items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: In fact he was a doll. In fact I was even his guest in the Unites States Senate later on.

ctx.x: Chilton has you going from -- let's see, the Paramount Hotel Grill in '33 to the following year, Park Central Hotel, '34, and then he says Glenn Allen Casino, Glen Island Hotel Roosevelt, New Orleans, et cetera.

Well, the Roosevelt Hotel came after, directly after, the Park Central. I remember we were there New Years Eve of '34 going into '35. And we were the first out of town band to play the room, and it was -- we used to play the dinner session in the Fountain Room, and Huey Long used to be in there every night for dinner. And he had these bodyguards around him, and they would sit, facing the backs of the chairs, looking around the rest of the room, and Huey would stuff his napkin in his neck and eat up a storm and…
Some book says that Huey Long complained that the band was too loud and that the management told you to play softer and you wouldn't.
